title: S3-SW-09 D3S END-TO-END SIMULATOR AND CONSTELLATION DESIGN
description: This activity aims to provide a key enabling tool to support the design and implementation planning of ESA's Distributed Space Weather Sensor System (D3S). The first part of the activity focuses on the development of a generic end-to-end mission simulator capableof assessing the performance of distributed space weather sensing architectures. The second part leverages the developed simulator to investigate and optimise the design of a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellation for space weather monitoring. Finally, the activity will assess and trade off different implementation options for the proposed constellation, including alternative payload configurations, dedicated satellites, and hosted payload opportunities

title: ULTRACOMPACT 778 NM RUBIDIUM SECONDARY OPTICAL FREQUENCY STANDARD - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to develop an ultracompact, secondary, optical frequency reference based on a two-photon transition in Rb vapour at 778nm.Description:Ultra-stable miniature atomic clocks are being considered for space applications. The Rubidium two-photon transition secondary frequency standard has demonstrated interesting performance metrics with a further potential for ultra-low size, weight and power (SWaP) integration.Currently, such an approach is hindered by the lack of miniaturized laser sources with suitable power levels and spectral properties as well as a compact physics package design taking advantage of the full capabilities of the integrated photonics and microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) gas cell technology platforms.This activity aims at exploiting these enabling technologies and developing a further concept of a compact high-performance atomic physics package for an ultra-compact secondary optical frequency standard. The goal of this activity is to provide a fractional frequency stability < 10 - 12 at 1 second integration time implemented using integrated photonic techniques.The following tasks are foreseen in this activity: Evaluate sources of integrated photonic laser systems delivering the wavelengths and the required spectral properties for the defined system approach. Develop Rb cell techniques and technologies targeting an ultracompact 778 nm rubidium secondary optical frequency standard using chip-scale photonic integration. Demonstrate the fractional stability performance achievable using the chosen chip-scale photonic approach. Evaluate chip-scale optical frequency combs with SiN Kerr comb techniques to provide an initial stabilized direct optical-RF link. Provide a packaging solution to maintain the preliminary performance achieved.NOTE: This activityis currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The finallist of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: RADIOISOTOPE THERMOELECTRIC GENERATOR THERMAL MANAGEMENT SYSTEM - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a passive thermal system to regulate the Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator temperature and to provide excess heat to the spacecraft/lander heat management system.Description: For exploration missions, there is a need (In situ resource utilization, deep space missions, long night survival...) to use efficient power generation systems as an alternative to solar panels. Europe is already engaged in developing a Radioisotope Heater Unit (RHU) and the next step is to develop bigger capabilities witha Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (RTG). As RTG is generating significant waste heat, there is an interest to reuse this heatand optimize the thermal control system, hence the whole system. Several thermal management systems with heat recovery are currently under study with the potential capability of receiving waste heat form RHU or RTG. However, interfacing with an RTG and regulatingits temperature is complex and requires a dedicated system for this unit. The goal of the activity is to develop a passive thermal system that regulates the temperature of the RTG and be able to provide excess heat to the spacecraft/lander heat management system viaa dedicated thermal interface. The RTG thermal system requires to operate with less than 5% of the electrical power generated bytheRTG. The heat recovery and the distribution of the RTG thermal energy would increase the overall efficiency of the system by more than 20%. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements consolidation - Technology trade off review - Design and manufacturing of a breadboard demonstrator - Validation testing of the breadboard demonstrator - Way forward for industrializationDeliverables: Breadboard, ReportProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activities in open competition limited to the-non-Large-System Integrators. title: S2-LT-04 + S2-LT-05 DEMONSTRATION OF THE OPERATIONAL CAPABILITY, ROBUSTNESS ENHANCEMENT AND MARKET READINESS OF NETWORKED LASER DEBRIS TRACKING - EXPRO +
description: The activity aims to mature and expand the Debris Laser Tracking Network toward operational readiness and market applicability. It focuses on improving automation, system performance, product accuracy, and end-user alignment, while also addressing legal and regulatory constraints for compliant laser ranging operations, including potential ranging to active satellites.The network will be expanded by integrating at least one additional Satellite Laser Ranging station, upgraded to support debris laser ranging also during daytime, to improve station automation, and to interface with the DLTN automation framework.A coordinated observation campaign, involving end users and the ESA Laser Ranging Station, will validate the enhanced operational concepts, demonstrate improved network performance, and assess the benefits of simultaneous operations across multiple debris ranging stations. The activity will deliver technical notes, market concepts, observation data, software, and station hardware upgrades over an 18-months contract period
